This is a read-only analysis of `ASK_GUARDPOSE_S262.md`, `GuardPose.gd`, and the relevant `FightStagePlayer.gd` windows. No files were edited and no engine/render tests were run. Numerical recommendations below are **proposed authoring and acceptance values**, not measurements of the current MetaHuman meshes or established universal boxing standards.

**1. Two-bone IK, authored poses, and what shipped games establish**

Use three complementary layers:

| Layer | Owns |
|---|---|
| Authored style pose | Stance, shoulder placement, chest shape, chin tuck, elbow bend plane, forearm roll, fist orientation |
| Constrained arm IK | Wrist placement, proportion adaptation, small variations, face/body clearance |
| Deformation correction | Elbow volume, forearm twisting, shoulder/armpit shape |

Create one approved full-body reference pose per style first. Then author a few nearby variants—compact/open, relaxed/defensive—and interpolate within that style. Small procedural variation can produce many distinct guards from these references.

The immediate problem in the inspected code is more fundamental than a poor choice of wrist target:

- `FightStagePlayer.gd:130–136` translates a bone relative to its parent.
- Fatigue compensates wrist positions with that operation at lines 283–284.
- Guard lift translates the hands at lines 289–290.
- Glove springs translate them at lines 295–296.
- Strike clearance translates the guarding hand at line 4126.

**Moving `LeftHand` relative to `LeftLowerArm` changes the elbow-to-wrist segment vector and potentially its length.** That is not equivalent to bending an arm. A well-positioned wrist can therefore coexist with a stretched or distorted forearm.

`_tuck_elbow()` is more defensible: rotating the upper-arm subtree around the shoulder-to-wrist axis can swivel the elbow while preserving the wrist position. However, it preserves the chain it receives—including any preceding wrist translation—and does not solve deformation or forearm-roll constraints.

For the replacement, accumulate fatigue, guard height, breathing compensation, and glove spring into **effector targets**, then solve the arm once. Do not translate the hand afterward.

Public evidence supports authored motion, but not an exact claim about either game’s guard solver:

- Steel City Interactive describes capturing fighters’ movement and having animation teams process and apply that motion to the models. That supports a mocap/authored foundation for **Undisputed**; it does not disclose a head-relative guard IK implementation. ## (b) Frame-by-frame: what makes the motion not look human

### Feet / stance — the worst offender
- **t = 1.0 s (BEFORE):** the red lead boxer stands in an exaggerated **lunge** — front foot planted far forward, rear leg almost straight, **heel lifted, both feet flat and splayed outward** (duck-footed). AFTER narrows the stance and stands him more upright, **but keeps the flat splay and the raised heel.**
- **t ≈ 7.9–8.0 s (AFTER):** red pitches forward onto the lead leg with the **trailing rear leg stretched out behind and off the floor** — a foot with no ground contact at all. Reads as falling, not footwork.
- **t ≈ 13.5–14.0 s:** the same forward lunge / rear-leg-straight-back-and-high silhouette returns (both halves).
- **Dense sample, t = 4.90 → 5.05 → 5.20 → 5.35 → 5.50 → 5.65 s:** the foot-contact regions **translate smoothly with the body** — there is no lift-then-plant. The **cast shadow** (the best ground-contact readout in this light) **sweeps continuously across the floor and never stops**. That is the skating signature.
- Feet are almost never **up on the balls**; there is no pivot.

### Hips / root
- The **pelvis moves in lockstep with the chest** — no pelvis-vs-shoulder counter-rotation in any sampled frame. At **t = 5.20 s and 5.50 s** (the cross) the whole torso+hips **hinges forward as one block** (“poured forward, hinged at the hip”).
- **Root height is essentially constant across stance changes:** at t = 1.0 the stance is far wider than at t = 5.5 yet the hip height is identical → the legs are being **posed under a floating root**, with no crouch/weight-drop.

### Spacing between the two men
- The gap **snaps** open and shut: heads overlapping at **t ≈ 5.2 s and 8.0 s**, a full body apart at **t ≈ 11.0 and 14.0 s**, inside ~0.3–0.5 s — and **neither man steps to close**; one root just translates.
- **Interpenetration:** at **t ≈ 8.0 s (AFTER)** blue’s glove/forearm passes **inside red’s head silhouette**; at **t ≈ 5.2 s** the two heads occupy the same screen space. There is no “measuring” distance.

### Guard (arms, elbows, gloves)
- **t = 4.90–5.20 s:** red’s **lead arm is fully extended low-and-left, nearly straight at the elbow, glove pointing down-left at nothing, and it stays there ~0.3 s** while he “slips.” The lead never returns to the face. **This is present in BOTH halves** — the one-root-solver change did not touch the guard.
- **Elbows flare out from the ribs** whenever the arm is out (t = 1.0 BEFORE; t = 4.90 both).
- **Gloves drift low** — the lead glove sits at sternum/waist height at **t ≈ 8.0 s and 14.0 s** (the “floating glove”).
- Gloves **don’t present knuckles** (palms read down/flat), and when both are up (**t = 5.6 s**) they **overlap the face and each other** rather than framing the chin.

### Punches
- **No wind-up:** at 4.90 → 5.05 the lead hand is **already extended** before the cross; the cross at **5.20 s** arrives with the shoulder already forward — no hip/shoulder wind-up and **no weight transfer** onto the lead foot.
- **Extension:** stiff, straight arm, **no shoulder rotating over the top** → it reads as a pole extending, not a punch.
- **Recovery:** 5.35 → 5.65 returns the hand to the **same low hang**, not to the chin.
- Same form repeats at **t ≈ 13.5–14.0 s**.

### Head movement
- **The head is welded to the trunk:** torso pitch carries the head (t = 1.0 BEFORE; t = 5.20) — no cervical counter-rotation. The “slip” at 5.2 is a **whole-body lean**, not a head slip. The chin never tucks behind the shoulder.

### Weight shift
- **Lean without centre-of-mass transfer:** the body pitches but the CoM doesn’t move over the lead foot, so punches have no push. At **t ≈ 8.0 s (AFTER)** the weight goes nowhere — pitched forward with the rear leg airborne.

### Be fair to the AFTER half
It **did** improve: the stance is narrower and more upright, the extreme splayed lunge of BEFORE is reduced, and spacing is slightly more consistent. But every fundamental tell — **skate, no step, dead lead arm, hinged hip, welded head, straight-arm punch, no recovery-to-guard** — is **the same in both halves**. The change is **root-motion/authoring unification, not motion quality.** That matches the code: `FightStagePlayer.gd` still poses the arm by **translating the Hand bone** (`_anim_translate_world`, line 130, applied to the hands at 283–296 for fatigue/lift/glove-spring) and swivelling the elbow (`_tuck_elbow`, 170) — a well-positioned wrist can coexist with a stretched forearm.

**Caveat I won’t paper over:** these are discrete samples (0.1–0.5 s apart, 0.15 s in the punch window). I can call *poses and contact* confidently; I cannot call *timing/feel*, and I could not measure world-space slip. That needs the foot probe in item 2.

4291: static func elbow_swivel_to_flare(shoulder: Vector3, elbow: Vector3, wrist: Vector3, torso_up: Vector3, outward: Vector3,
4292: 		want_flare: float, limit: float) -> Vector3:
4293: 	var axis: Vector3 = (wrist - shoulder).normalized()
4294: 	if axis.length() < 0.5:
4295: 		return elbow
4296: 	var best: Vector3 = elbow
4297: 	var best_d: float = absf(arm_flare_deg(shoulder, elbow, torso_up, outward) - want_flare)
4298: 	var deg: float = 2.0
4299: 	while deg <= limit:
4300: 		for sgn in [1.0, -1.0]:
4301: 			var e: Vector3 = shoulder + Basis(axis, deg_to_rad(deg * sgn)) * (elbow - shoulder)
4302: 			var d: float = absf(arm_flare_deg(shoulder, e, torso_up, outward) - want_flare)
4303: 			if d < best_d - 0.25:

4305: 				best = e

1: extends RefCounted
2: ## S261 GUARD POSE (operator: "it's just a guard pose and we need a shit ton of variations of that"). The guard is no longer the
3: ## clip's arm (a retargeted take that does not fit the MetaHuman - flared lead elbow, rear glove in the cheek, "doesn't look like
4: ## an arm") patched by layers: it is a handful of numbers per boxer, and FightStagePlayer's two-bone IK puts each wrist on its
5: ## target with the elbow aimed down/in at the ribs. Pure: zero preloads, every input passed in.
6: ##
7: ## FRAME: offsets are metres in the boxer's HEAD frame - origin the Head bone (skull base), f = where his chest faces, r = his
8: ## right, u = up. Orthodox: LEAD = left hand. Southpaw mirrors r.
9: ## Sources: Ludo LUDO_ELBOW_S261 (wrist 0.21-0.23 m from the head bone, glove 6-8 cm in front of the chin, elbow 3-5 cm off the
10: ## ribs, upper arm 8-12 deg from vertical); Undisputed TRAD idles (both elbows near-symmetric); our measured idle (rear 0.31 m,
11: ## lead 0.43 m - too far, the "floating" glove).
12: 
13: const STYLES := {
14: 	## Hands high, rear glove at the chin, lead a forearm in front of the eyes.
15: 	"high_guard": {"rear": Vector3(0.150, 0.075, -0.150), "lead": Vector3(0.260, -0.060, -0.090), "pole_fwd": 0.20, "pole_in": 0.45},
16: 	## Both gloves at the cheekbones, elbows glued to the ribs.
17: 	"peekaboo": {"rear": Vector3(0.140, 0.085, -0.110), "lead": Vector3(0.150, -0.085, -0.110), "pole_fwd": 0.15, "pole_in": 0.55},
18: 	## Lead arm long to measure distance, rear at the chin.
19: 	"long_guard": {"rear": Vector3(0.160, 0.070, -0.160), "lead": Vector3(0.380, -0.040, -0.160), "pole_fwd": 0.25, "pole_in": 0.35},
20: 	## Philly shell: lead hand low across the belly, rear glove at the chin, lead shoulder up.

# godot_hidden.ps1 - run a WINDOWED Godot job without it popping up on the operator's screen.
#
# Operator, 2026-09-23: "can you make the windows that the agents open do not pop and run
# silently in the background". Render tools cannot run --headless (no GPU output), and Godot
# CLAMPS both `--position` and DisplayServer.window_set_position() back onto a visible monitor
# (measured: --position 20000,20000 landed at 1486,761; a script move to -32000 read back 0,0).
# So the hiding is done from OUTSIDE: start Godot, wait for its window, then Win32 SetWindowPos
# it to -32000,-32000 (off every monitor, NOT minimized - a minimized Godot stops drawing, so
# captures would come out empty), no activation, and drop its taskbar button.
#
# S133 (operator 2026-09-30, during two S133 recordings: "can you make the debug popup stop"):
# the window titled "... (DEBUG)" still reached the screen. Two holes: (1) the watch loop ran a
# CIM process query every 50 ms pass, so the first hide came late; (2) each window was hidden
# ONCE, and Godot moves its own window afterwards (movie mode resizes 1280x720 -> 1920x1080 and
# re-centres it), which put it back on the monitor for the rest of the job. Now the loop checks
# every 15 ms against a cached pid list and re-hides ANY visible window of the job whose left
# edge is back on a monitor. FIGHTCAMP_HIDDEN_TRACE=1 prints each hide (ms since start, rect).
#
# Usage (all Godot args after the script path are passed through unchanged):
#   powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File Tools\godot_hidden.ps1 --path Godot --script tools/x.gd -- arg=1
# Exit code is Godot's. Output (stdout+stderr) is streamed to this console.

$ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"
$godot = Join-Path $env:LOCALAPPDATA "Programs\Godot\Godot_v4.7.2-stable_win64_console.exe"

if ($godot -match '_console\.exe$') { $gui = $godot -replace '_console\.exe$', '.exe'; if (Test-Path $gui) { $godot = $gui } }

# GDScript traps that cost a fix cycle (moved from CLAUDE.md s9, S213)

- `var x := <call>` fails when the call returns Variant - type it (`var n: int = ...`). `%` in a format string is `%%`.
- A variable name reused in one function is a parse error, even across blocks.
- `remove_child(node)` before `queue_free()` on UI rebuilds. A Label outside a Container: break lines with `\n`.
- Full-rect-anchored Controls: never assign `size` on mount. TextureRect: set `expand_mode`/`stretch_mode` BEFORE texture.
- Scene scripts compiled before autoloads use `get_node_or_null("/root/GameState")`, never the bare identifier.
- `callv` with the wrong arity returns `{}`, not null. Headless `get_bone_global_pose()` needs the skeleton updated.
- A Label that has already grown to its text never shrinks back: set `clip_text`/overrun BEFORE `size` (S213 STRESSHDR1).

#
# Operator, 2026-09-23: "can you make the windows that the agents open do not pop and run

# CLAMPS both `--position` and DisplayServer.window_set_position() back onto a visible monitor
# (measured: --position 20000,20000 landed at 1486,761; a script move to -32000 read back 0,0).
# So the hiding is done from OUTSIDE: start Godot, wait for its window, then Win32 SetWindowPos
# it to -32000,-32000 (off every monitor, NOT minimized - a minimized Godot stops drawing, so

# edge is back on a monitor. FIGHTCAMP_HIDDEN_TRACE=1 prints each hide (ms since start, rect).

# Systematic Debugging

## Overview

**Core principle:** ALWAYS find root cause before attempting fixes. Symptom fixes are failure.

**Violating the letter of this process is violating the spirit of debugging.**

## The Iron Law

'''
NO FIXES WITHOUT ROOT CAUSE INVESTIGATION FIRST
'''

If you haven't completed Phase 1, you cannot propose fixes.

## When to Use

Use for ANY technical issue:
- Test failures
- Bugs in production
- Unexpected behavior
- Performance problems
- Build failures
- Integration issues

**Use this ESPECIALLY when:**
- Under time pressure (emergencies make guessing tempting)
- "Just one quick fix" seems obvious
- You've already tried multiple fixes
- Previous fix didn't work
- You don't fully understand the issue

**Don't skip when:**
- Issue seems simple (simple bugs have root causes too)
- You're in a hurry (rushing guarantees rework)
- Manager wants it fixed NOW (systematic is faster than thrashing)

## Retargeting 3D Skeletons
### To share animations among multiple Skeletons
Godot has Position/Rotation/Scale 3D tracks (which this document calls "Transform" tracks)
with Nodepaths to bones for Skeleton bone animation. This means you can't
share animations between multiple Skeletons just by using the same bone
names.

Godot allows each bone to have a parent-child relationship and can have rotation
and scale as well as position, which means that bones that share a name can still
have different Transform values.

The Skeleton stores the Transform values necessary for the default pose as Bone Rest.
If Bone Pose is equal to Bone Rest, it means that the Skeleton is in the default pose.

.. note:: Godot 3 and Godot 4 have different Bone Pose behaviors.
          In Godot 3, Bone Pose is relative to Bone Rest, but in Godot 4,
          it includes Bone Rest. See this
          `article <https://godotengine.org/article/animation-data-redesign-40>`__
          for more information.

Skeletal models have different Bone Rests depending on the environment from
which they were exported. For example, the bones of a glTF model output from Blender
have "Edit Bone Orientation" as the Bone Rest rotation. However, there are skeletal
models without any Bone Rest rotations, such as the glTF model output from Maya.

To share animations in Godot, it is necessary to match Bone Rests as well as Bone Names
to remove unwanted tracks in some cases. You can do that using the scene importer.

### Bone Map
When you select the Skeleton3D node in the advanced scene import menu, a menu will appear
on the right-hand side containing the "Retarget" section. The Retarget section has a single
property ``bone_map``.

.. image:: img/retargeting1.webp

With the Skeleton node selected, first set up a new :ref:`class_bonemap` and :ref:`class_skeletonprofile`.
Godot has a preset called :ref:`class_skeletonprofilehumanoid` for humanoid models.
This tutorial proceeds with the assumption that you are using :ref:`class_skeletonprofilehumanoid`.

.. note:: If you need a profile that is different from :ref:`class_skeletonprofilehumanoid`, you can export
          a :ref:`class_skeletonprofile` from the editor by selecting a Skeleton3D and using the **Skeleton3D** menu in the 3D viewport's toolbar.

When you use :ref:`class_skeletonprofilehumanoid`, auto-mapping will be performed when the
:ref:`class_skeletonprofile` is set. If the auto-mapping does not work well, you can map bones manually.

.. image:: img/retargeting2.webp

Any missing, duplicate or incorrect parent-child relationship mappings will be indicated
by a magenta / red button (depending on the editor setting). It does not block the import process,
but it warns that animations may not be shared correctly.

.. note:: The auto-mapping uses pattern matching for the bone names. So we recommend
          to use common English names for bones.

After you set up the ``bone_map``, several options are available in the sections below.

## Command line tutorial
### Command line tutorial
.. highlight:: shell

Some developers like using the command line extensively. Godot is
designed to be friendly to them, so here are the steps for working
entirely from the command line. Given the engine relies on almost no
external libraries, initialization times are pretty fast, making it
suitable for this workflow.

.. note::

    On Windows and Linux, you can run a Godot binary in a terminal by specifying
    its relative or absolute path.

    On macOS, the process is different due to Godot being contained within a
    ``.app`` bundle (which is a *folder*, not a file). To run a Godot binary
    from a terminal on macOS, you have to ``cd`` to the folder where the Godot
    application bundle is located, then run ``Godot.app/Contents/MacOS/Godot``
    followed by any command line arguments. If you've renamed the application
    bundle from ``Godot`` to another name, make sure to edit this command line
    accordingly.

### Path
It is recommended to place your Godot editor binary in your ``PATH`` environment
variable, so it can be executed easily from any place by typing ``godot``.
You can do so on Linux by placing the Godot binary in ``/usr/local/bin`` and
making sure it is called ``godot`` (case-sensitive).

To achieve this on Windows or macOS easily, you can install Godot using
`Scoop <https://scoop.sh>`__ (on Windows) or `Homebrew <https://brew.sh>`__
(on macOS). This will automatically make the copy of Godot installed
available in the ``PATH``:

.. tabs::

 .. code-tab:: sh Windows

    # Add "Extras" bucket
    scoop bucket add extras

    # Standard editor:
    scoop install godot

    # Editor with C# support (will be available as `godot-mono` in `PATH`):
    scoop install godot-mono

 .. code-tab:: sh macOS

    # Standard editor:
    brew install godot

    # Editor with C# support (will be available as `godot-mono` in `PATH`):
    brew install godot-mono

### Running a script
It is possible to run a ``.gd`` script from the command line.
This feature is especially useful in large projects, e.g. for batch
conversion of assets or custom import/export.

The script must inherit from ``SceneTree`` or ``MainLoop``.

Here is an example ``sayhello.gd``, showing how it works:

.. code-block:: python

    #!/usr/bin/env -S godot -s
    extends SceneTree

    func _init():
        print("Hello!")
        quit()

And how to run it:

::

    # Prints "Hello!" to standard output.
    godot -s sayhello.gd

If no ``project.godot`` exists at the path, current path is assumed to be the
current working directory (unless ``--path`` is specified).

The script path will be interpreted as a resource path relative to
the project, here ``res://sayhello.gd``. You can also use an absolute
filesystem path instead, which is useful if the script is located
outside of the project directory.

The first line of ``sayhello.gd`` above is commonly referred to as
a *shebang*. If the Godot binary is in your ``PATH`` as ``

18: 	## Release: a punching arm reaches 0 in GUARD_IK_RELEASE_S, not sooner; the guard arm never moves.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Parse gate for GDScript: runs Godot --check-only on each file.

Usage (from anywhere):
  python Godot/tools/check_scripts.py                       # every scripts/*.gd and tests/*.gd
  python Godot/tools/check_scripts.py scripts/GameState.gd tests/smoke_test.gd
  python Godot/tools/check_scripts.py --strict-autoloads ...

About one second per file; exit 1 if any file fails. Catches what the
parser and analyzer catch: syntax errors, "inferred from a Variant value",
redeclared variables, unknown members on typed values. It does not run the
code, so runtime errors (bad format strings, missing nodes) still need the
tests. A parse error that reaches a headless test HANGS the test until its
timeout instead of failing it, so run this before any test run.

The check runs before the autoloads exist, so "Compile Error: Identifier
not found: GameState" (or any other [autoload] name in project.godot) is
expected noise and is filtered; such a script passes when no other error
remains. Preloaded modules under scripts/ emit a distinct warning for that
noise; --strict-autoloads makes those warnings fatal. Set GODOT_EXE to override
the executable path.
"""
import glob
import os
import re
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import time

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
PROJECT = os.path.dirname(HERE)  # .../Godot

def _no_console(path: str) -> str:
    """S166 (operator 2026-10-05: "please no popups on my other monitor", the window was a black console):
    on Windows 11 the *_console.exe shim is handed to Windows Terminal, which opens on the operator's
    monitor whatever flags or desktop the caller gives it. Always run the GUI sibling; it still writes
    to redirected stdout/stderr (measured S166: --headless output reaches the pipes)."""
    if path.lower().endswith("_console.exe"):
        sibling = path[:-len("_console.exe")] + ".exe"
        if os.path.isfile(sibling):
            return sibling
    return path

## Paired same-seed 30 fps guard IK/control measurement. Runs the approved live-fight probe twice;
## only the control has FightStagePlayer.guard_ik disabled. Emits release/return windows per punch.

func _arg(key: String, fallback: String = "") -> String:
	for arg: String in OS.get_cmdline_user_args():
		if arg.begins_with(key + "="):
			return arg.trim_prefix(key + "=")
	return fallback


func _run_case(label: String, ik: bool, report: String, still_dir: String) -> bool:
	var args: PackedStringArray = ["--path", ProjectSettings.globalize_path("res://"), "--fixed-fps", "30", "--script", "tools/guard_lift_still.gd", "--", "as_game", "out=" + still_dir, "report=" + report, "style_a=peekaboo", "style_b=high_guard", "attributes=0", "elbow_log=0", "guard_ik=" + ("1" if ik else "0")]
	var output: Array = []
	var code: int = OS.execute(OS.get_executable_path(), args, output, true)
	var text: String = "\n".join(PackedStringArray(output))
	print("GUARD_POP_CASE %s ik=%s exit=%d\n%s" % [label, str(ik), code, text])
	return code == 0 and FileAccess.file_exists(report)


func _load_samples(path: String) -> Dictionary:
	var file: FileAccess = FileAccess.open(path, FileAccess.READ)
	if file == null:
		return {}
	var parsed: Variant = JSON.parse_string(file.get_as_text())
	return parsed as Dictionary if parsed is Dictionary else {}


func _vec(row: Dictionary) -> Vector3:
	var p: Array = row.get("wrist", [])
	return Vector3(float(p[0]), float(p[1]), float(p[2])) if p.size() == 3 else Vector3.ZERO


func _initialize() -> void:
	var base: String = _arg("out", "")
	if base.is_empty():
		push_error("out=<absolute directory> required")
		quit(2)
		return
	DirAccess.make_dir_recursive_absolute(base)
	var guarded_path: String = base.path_join("guarded.json")
	var control_path: String = base.path_join("control.json")
	var guarded_stills: String = base.path_join("guarded")
	var control_stills: String = base.path_join("control")
	DirAccess.make_dir_recursive_absolute(guarded_stills)
	DirAccess.make_dir_recursive_absolute(control_stills)
	if not _run_case("guarded", true, guarded_path, guarded_stills) or not _run_case("control", false, control_path, control_stills):
		push_error("paired run failed")
		quit(1)

## RetargetModifier3D
A modifier to transfer parent skeleton poses (or global poses) to child skeletons in model space with different rests.

Retrieves the pose (or global pose) relative to the parent Skeleton's rest in model space and transfers it to the child Skeleton. This modifier rewrites the pose of the child skeleton directly in the parent skeleton's update process. This means that it overwrites the mapped bone pose set in the normal process on the target skeleton. If you want to set the target skeleton bone pose after retargeting, you will need to add a [SkeletonModifier3D] child to the target skeleton and thereby modify the pose. [b]Note:[/b] When the [member use_global_pose] is enabled, even if it is an unmapped bone, it can cause visual problems because the global pose is applied ignoring the parent bone's pose [b]if it has mapped bone children[/b]. See also [member use_global_pose].
- use_global_pose() -> bool
  If [code]false[/code], in case the target skeleton has fewer bones than the source skeleton, the source bone parent's transform will be ignored. Instead, it is possible to retarget between models with different body shapes, and position, rotation, and scale can be retargeted separately. If [code]true[/code], retargeting is performed taking into account global pose. In case the target skeleton has fewer bones than the source skeleton, the source bone parent's transform is taken into account. However, bone length between skeletons must match exactly, if not, the bones will be forced to expand or shrink. This is useful for using dummy bone with length [code]0[/code] to match postures when retargeting between models with different number of bones.
- set_position_enabled(enabled) -> void
  Sets [constant TRANSFORM_FLAG_POSITION] into [member enable].
- set_rotation_enabled(enabled) -> void
  Sets [constant TRANSFORM_FLAG_ROTATION] into [member enable].
- set_scale_enabled(enabled) -> void
  Sets [constant TRANSFORM_FLAG_SCALE] into [member enable].
- enable() -> int — Flags to control the process of the transform elements individually when [member use_global_pose] is disabled.
- profile() -> SkeletonProfile — [SkeletonProfile] for retargeting bones with names matching the bone list.
- is_position_enabled() -> bool — Returns [code]true[/code] if [member enable] has [constant TRANSFORM_FLAG_POSITION].
- is_rotation_enabled() -> bool — Returns [code]true[/code] if [member enable] has [constant TRANSFORM_FLAG_ROTATION].
- is_scale_enabled() -> bool — Returns [code]true[/code] if [member enable] has [constant TRANSFORM_FLAG_SCALE].
- TRANSFORM_FLAG_POSITION() — If set, allows to retarget the position.
- TRANSFORM_FLAG_ROTATION() — If set, allows to retarget the rotation.
- TRANSFORM_FLAG_SCALE() — If set, allows to retarget the scale.
- TRANSFORM_FLAG_ALL() — If set, allows to retarget the position/rotation/scale.

**Use authored guard poses plus constrained two-bone IK.** Author the whole-body silhouette and arm roll; use IK to fit that pose to each boxer’s proportions and maintain glove clearance. Replacing wrist translations with IK should improve skeletal integrity, but IK alone cannot repair incorrect skin weights, missing corrective-joint behavior, or an incorrectly oriented glove.

This is a read-only analysis of `ASK_GUARDPOSE_S262.md`, `GuardPose.gd`, and the relevant `FightStagePlayer.gd` windows. No files were edited and no engine/render tests were run. Numerical recommendations below are **proposed authoring and acceptance values**, not measurements of the current MetaHuman meshes or established universal boxing standards.

**1. Two-bone IK, authored poses, and what shipped games establish**

Use three complementary layers:

| Layer | Owns |
|---|---|
| Authored style pose | Stance, shoulder placement, chest shape, chin tuck, elbow bend plane, forearm roll, fist orientation |
| Constrained arm IK | Wrist placement, proportion adaptation, small variations, face/body clearance |
| Deformation correction | Elbow volume, forearm twisting, shoulder/armpit shape |

Create one approved full-body reference pose per style first. Then author a few nearby variants—compact/open, relaxed/defensive—and interpolate within that style. Small procedural variation can produce many distinct guards from these references.

The immediate problem in the inspected code is more fundamental than a poor choice of wrist target:

- `FightStagePlayer.gd:130–136` translates a bone relative to its parent.
- Fatigue compensates wrist positions with that operation at lines 283–284.
- Guard lift translates the hands at lines 289–290.
- Glove springs translate them at lines 295–296.
- Strike clearance translates the guarding hand at line 4126.

**Moving `LeftHand` relative to `LeftLowerArm` changes the elbow-to-wrist segment vector and potentially its length.** That is not equivalent to bending an arm. A well-positioned wrist can therefore coexist with a stretched or distorted forearm.

`_tuck_elbow()` is more defensible: rotating the upper-arm subtree around the shoulder-to-wrist axis can swivel the elbow while preserving the wrist position. However, it preserves the chain it receives—including any preceding wrist translation—and does not solve deformation or forearm-roll constraints.

For the replacement, accumulate fatigue, guard height, breathing compensation, and glove spring into **effector targets**, then solve the arm once. Do not translate the hand afterward.

Public evidence supports authored motion, but not an exact claim about either game’s guard solver:

- Steel City Interactive describes capturing fighters’ movement and having animation teams process and apply that motion to the models. That supports a mocap/authored foundation for **Undisputed**; it does not disclose a head-relative guard IK implementation. [Steel City Interactive’s development account](https://blog.

stuck. When they say "just guess" or "what do you think?", propose

said in plain words. When there's existing work, build on what it already
uses. Any choice you make goes in the design as your call, never as

# Antigravity CLI (`agy`) Tool Mapping

Skills speak in actions ("dispatch a subagent", "create a todo", "read a file"). On the Antigravity CLI (`agy`) these resolve to the tools below.

| Action skills request | Antigravity CLI equivalent |
|----------------------|----------------------|
| Dispatch a subagent (`Subagent (general-purpose):` template) | `invoke_subagent` with a built-in `TypeName` — `self` for full-capability work, `research` for read-only |
| Task tracking ("create a todo", "mark complete") | a **task artifact** — `write_to_file` with `IsArtifact: true` and `ArtifactType: "task"` (see [Task tracking](#task-tracking)). **Not** `manage_task`, which manages background processes. |

## Task tracking

Antigravity has **no todo tool** (`manage_task` manages background
processes — `list`/`kill`/`status`/`send_input` — it is *not* a checklist). When a

## Retargeting 3D Skeletons
### To share animations among multiple Skeletons
Godot has Position/Rotation/Scale 3D tracks (which this document calls "Transform" tracks)
with Nodepaths to bones for Skeleton bone animation. This means you can't
share animations between multiple Skeletons just by using the same bone
names.

Godot allows each bone to have a parent-child relationship and can have rotation
and scale as well as position, which means that bones that share a name can still
have different Transform values.

The Skeleton stores the Transform values necessary for the default pose as Bone Rest.
If Bone Pose is equal to Bone Rest, it means that the Skeleton is in the default pose.

.. note:: Godot 3 and Godot 4 have different Bone Pose behaviors.
          In Godot 3, Bone Pose is relative to Bone Rest, but in Godot 4,
          it includes Bone Rest. See this
          `article <https://godotengine.org/article/animation-data-redesign-40>`__
          for more information.

Skeletal models have different Bone Rests depending on the environment from
which they were exported. For example, the bones of a glTF model output from Blender
have "Edit Bone Orientation" as the Bone Rest rotation. However, there are skeletal
models without any Bone Rest rotations, such as the glTF model output from Maya.

To share animations in Godot, it is necessary to match Bone Rests as well as Bone Names
to remove unwanted tracks in some cases. You can do that using the scene importer.

### Bone Map
When you select the Skeleton3D node in the advanced scene import menu, a menu will appear
on the right-hand side containing the "Retarget" section. The Retarget section has a single
property ``bone_map``.

.. image:: img/retargeting1.webp

With the Skeleton node selected, first set up a new :ref:`class_bonemap` and :ref:`class_skeletonprofile`.
Godot has a preset called :ref:`class_skeletonprofilehumanoid` for humanoid models.
This tutorial proceeds with the assumption that you are using :ref:`class_skeletonprofilehumanoid`.

.. note:: If you need a profile that is different from :ref:`class_skeletonprofilehumanoid`, you can export
          a :ref:`class_skeletonprofile` from the editor by selecting a Skeleton3D and using the **Skeleton3D** menu in the 3D viewport's toolbar.

When you use :ref:`class_skeletonprofilehumanoid`, auto-mapping will be performed when the
:ref:`class_skeletonprofile` is set. If the auto-mapping does not work well, you can map bones manually.

.. image:: img/retargeting2.webp

Any missing, duplicate or incorrect parent-child relationship mappings will be indicated
by a magenta / red button (depending on the editor setting). It does not block the import process,
but it warns that animations may not be shared correctly.

.. note:: The auto-mapping uses pattern matching for the bone names. So we recommend
          to use common English names for bones.

After you set up the ``bone_map``, several options are available in the sections below.

## GDScript reference
### Static variables
A class member variable can be declared static:

::

    static var a

Static variables belong to the class, not instances. This means that static variables
share values between multiple instances, unlike regular member variables.

From inside a class, you can access static variables from any function, both static and non-static.
From outside the class, you can access static variables using the class or an instance
(the second is not recommended as it is less readable).

.. note::

    The ``@export`` and ``@onready`` annotations cannot be applied to a static variable.
    Local variables cannot be static.

The following example defines a ``Person`` class with a static variable named ``max_id``.
We increment the ``max_id`` in the ``_init()`` function. This makes it easy to keep track
of the number of ``Person`` instances in our game.

::

    # person.gd
    class_name Person

    static var max_id = 0

    var id
    var name

    func _init(p_name):
        max_id += 1
        id = max_id
        name = p_name

In this code, we create two instances of our ``Person`` class and check that the class
and every instance have the same ``max_id`` value, because the variable is static and accessible to every instance.

::

    # test.gd
    extends Node

    func _ready():
        var person1 = Person.new("John Doe")
        var person2 = Person.new("Jane Doe")

        print(person1.id) # 1
        print(person2.id) # 2

        print(Person.max_id)  # 2
        print(person1.max_id) # 2
        print(person2.max_id) # 2

Static variables can have type hints, setters and getters:

::

    static var balance: int = 0

    static var debt: int:
        get:
            return -balance
        set(value):
            balance = -value

A base class static variable can also be accessed via a child class:

::

    class A:
        static var x = 1

    class B extends A:
        pass

    func _ready():
        prints(A.x, B.x) # 1 1
        A.x = 2
        prints(A.x, B.x) # 2 2
        B.x = 3
        prints(A.x, B.x) # 3 3

.. note::

    When referencing a static variable from a tool script, the other script
    containing the static variable **must** also be a tool script.
    See :ref:`Running code in the editor <doc_running_code_in_the_editor_important_information>`
    for details.

### Annotations
Annotations are special tokens in GDScript that act as modifiers to an entire script,
a declaration, a statement, or a location in the source code. Annotations may affect
how the script is treated by the Godot editor and the GDScript compiler.

Every annotation starts with the ``@`` character and is specified by a name. A
detailed description and example for each annotation can be found inside the
:ref:`GDScript class reference <class_@GDScript>`.

For instance, you can use it to export a value to the editor:

::

    @export_range(1, 100, 1, "or_greater")
    var ranged_var: int = 50
